proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 60, 4^n is congruent to 4^(n mod 13) modulo 23.

argument.text: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 47, 4^(n+13) mod 23 is congruent to 4^(n) mod 23 modulo 23.

For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 60, at least one of the following holds: n mod 13 = 0; n mod 13 = 1; n mod 13 = 2; n mod 13 = 3; n mod 13 = 4; n mod 13 = 5; n mod 13 = 6; n mod 13 = 7; n mod 13 = 8; n mod 13 = 9; n mod 13 = 10; n mod 13 = 11; n mod 13 = 12.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, 2*n^2 is congruent to (2*n^2) + 33 modulo 3.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 60 for which n^2 > 30.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, n^2 is at least n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, n^2 + n is congruent to (n^2 + n) + 391 modulo 17.
The steps above establish the statement up to 60, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 60.
